text:
mike_support: Heads up — escalation from AcmeCorp: their web client throws a SyntaxError when calling our streaming Responses API with structured output enabled. Happens intermittently for prompts that include backslashes and CRLFs in user-provided text.

mike_support: Customer error (browser console): "Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token \" in JSON at position 178". They paste the concatenated stream they tried to parse and it fails.

annie_custsuccess: They say it only fails when using stream=true. Non-streaming responses parse fine.

sara_eng: I reproduced locally. Root cause: our streaming serializer can emit escapes at chunk boundaries and we escape per-chunk which double-escapes backslashes when chunks are concatenated naïvely. Example from my capture:

```
# chunk A
{"type":"response.delta","delta":{"text":"Hello \"user\" said:\
This is line1\"}}
# chunk B
{"type":"response.delta","delta":{"text":"\nAnd a second line with backslash: \\\server\"}}"}```

When the client concatenates raw chunk payloads and tries JSON.parse it gets something like:

{"text":"Hello \\\"user\\\" said:\\nThis is line1\nAnd a second line with backslash: \\\\\\server\\\"}

Which has run-on escapes (too many backslashes) and some chunks break escape sequences (e.g., \"\\n\" split across boundary) — the browser parser interprets them incorrectly.

sara_eng: Short-term mitigation: advise the client to join the stream frames at the JSON object boundary level rather than simple string concat. If they control the client, they can buffer until they see a complete object ending with '}' before JSON.parse. Also a quick post-process hack: after concatenation, run .replace(/\\n/g, "\n") and .replace(/\\r/g, "\r") to collapse double-escapes, but it's brittle.

mike_support: Customer also noticed a spike in token usage because their client retries on parse error. Billing flagged ~3x token consumption for the last hour — billing-sheila looped in.

billing-sheila: I\'ve put a temporary credit hold and started an audit. We\'ll follow up once eng confirms root cause and estimated timeline for fix.

sara_eng: Long-term fix options:
- avoid per-chunk escaping on serializer; emit raw bytes for text fields and escape only on final object serialization
- or ensure chunk boundaries never split escape sequences by buffering a few bytes and merging if necessary
- better framing: send length-prefixed JSON or newline-delimited JSON so clients can detect complete frames easily

sara_eng: I\'ve opened an internal issue and a PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/842 (WIP) — changes to streaming serializer to buffer escapes across chunk boundaries. Assigning to eng-runtime for review.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-021, severity: high-impact for this customer only. Labels: streaming, structured-output, escape-encoding.

mike_support: Next steps — confirm PR ETA, notify customer of temporary workaround (buffer frames), and keep billing updated. I\'ll offer them a temporary credit until fix is deployed.

annie_custsuccess: Customer on a paid dedicated plan and considering private deploy; they want a patch timeline before they expand usage.

sara_eng: ETA for review is EOD tomorrow; if no blocker we can ship a hotfix build in 48-72 hrs. Will update INC-2026-021 and ping here.

mike_support: Thanks — please post a concise repro snippet I can send to the customer.

sara_eng: Repro snippet (node):

```
const es = require('eventsource'); // pseudo-example
let buffer = '';
es.on('message', (chunk) => {
  buffer += chunk; // naive concat -> broken
  try { console.log(JSON.parse(buffer)); buffer=''; } catch (e) {}
});

// Correct approach: detect full object boundary or use NDJSON framing
```

mike_support: OK sending this to AcmeCorp. I\'ll update thread once they test the buffering workaround.
